Description - CheckEvents

Periodic keep-alive/poll. Returns the current settings, the account balance and changes/folderModifyTime; when that tick count is newer than the local folder tree the client re-reads it with Folders(0,0). There is no event list: the new member was nil in every reply, including 15 probes right after uploads, ModifyFolder calls, SavePlaylist and folder removals (after-upload, after-saveplaylist), and the client never reads it (it looks up only accountBalance, settings and changes). Whether the server ever fills new: Unknown.

When the client sends it: right after a successful Auth, then on a single-shot timer whose period is the shortest one currently requested (default values): 300 s normally ([proto-box] check-events-period), 60 s while the uploader is busy (check-events-uploading-period), 15 s while a folder view is open (check-events-folders-period). Adding a shorter period sends CheckEvents at once. Session-bound and never retransmitted. After more than check-events-repeat-count (3) consecutive errors the client re-logs.

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/CheckEvents. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/CheckEvents) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/CheckEvents (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation CheckEvents. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/CheckEvents query.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

        • <token> string required Token

          Session token. Always the first child.

        • <stats> object optional CheckEventsStats

          Client state; always sent by the client, optional for the server.

          • <isUploading> boolean required

            An upload is in progress.

          • <isPlaying> boolean required

            The music player is playing.

          • <isDownloading> boolean required

            A download is in progress.

          • <panelSelectedTab> integer (int32) required

            Index of the tab selected in the main panel.

          • <animation> integer (int32) required

            Id of the mascot animation currently shown.

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check CheckEventsResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema CheckEventsResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required CheckEventsResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for CheckEvents: <s:Envelope><s:Body><CheckEventsResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><CheckEventsResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <CheckEventsResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <CheckEventsResult> object required CheckEventsResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. Serialised as <status xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl"> (default-namespace redeclaration, no prefix) in this result type.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise. Same namespace treatment as status.

          • <a:new> object | string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/TeamSolutions.Chomik.DAO.ChomikBox

            nil in every reply observed, including 15 probes right after uploads, ModifyFolder, SavePlaylist and folder removals; its type is unknown. The client never looks it up, so a value would be ignored.

          • <a:settings> object optional nullable (i:nil) Settings xmlns http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/TeamSolutions.Chomik.DAO.ChomikBox

            Current settings (downloadByBox is copied into [downloader] enabled).

            • <downloadByBox> boolean required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Whether downloads started on the web site are handed to ChomikBox. Mirrors [downloader] enabled in the client config.

          • <a:accountBalance> object optional nullable (i:nil) AccountBalance xmlns http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/TeamSolutions.Chomik.DAO.ChomikBox

            Current balance.

            • <transfer> object required nullable (i:nil) TransferBalance xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Transfer quota.

              • <value> integer (int64) required

                Remaining transfer in kB (the client shows it as MB after dividing by 1024; consistent with the live transfer agreement cost = size / 1024). Live value 51200 = 50 MB.

              • <limit> integer (int64) required

                Transfer limit in kB (live value 51200).

              • <extra> integer (int64) required

                Extra (purchased) transfer; presumably kB as well (Inferred).

            • <points> integer (int64) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Points balance.

          • <a:changes> object optional nullable (i:nil) FolderChanges xmlns http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/TeamSolutions.Chomik.DAO.ChomikBox

            Folder-tree change marker.

            • <b:folderModifyTime> integer (int64) required xmlns http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/TeamSolutions.Chomik.Library.DAO.ChomikBox

              Time of the last change of the folder tree in .NET ticks (100 ns since 0001-01-01). When newer than the local tree the client refreshes it with Folders(0,0). This is the only "event" the service reports.

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Examples text/xml (2)

Deserialization failed (HTTP 500, fault a:DeserializationFailed) response 500 deserialization-failed

Captured live on 2026-10-24T15:25:07Z: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8.

A value that cannot be parsed as the parameter type (Int32) gives a:DeserializationFailed naming the parameter; the operation body never runs. This oracle was used to discover every parameter name/type/order.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • Result has an extra new member (nil in every reply) that the client never reads.
  • Result uses the DAO datacontract namespace for a: and a third namespace for changes children; the client parses by local name so this is harmless.

Security notes - findings that concern CheckEvents

  • C-09 Info Usage data stats{isUploading, isPlaying, isDownloading, panelSelectedTab, animation} rides on every CheckEvents poll. BoxEvents is not off by default: it sends fixed events whenever they occur (shutdown = poweroff/suspend/quit, detected.defaultplayer, settings.defaultplayer, settings.autostart).
  • S-10 Info Concurrent sessions are allowed; Logout invalidates only its own token; no expiry was observed within about 45 minutes.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
